item.title: ABC News: Home owner felt 'physically ill' when she realised she was scammed
item.description: Bana D'Sena moved regionally for a quiet lifestyle, but instead she has been left $14,000 out of pocket.

item.title: ABC News: Use of police utes to transport bodies in Tennant Creek labelled inhumane
item.description: Residents and leaders are calling for the government to step in with a solution to stop caged police vehicles being used to transport dead bodies to the Tennant Creek morgue.

item.title: ABC News: Alexander Zverev officially notified of lawsuit by ex-partner in abuse case
item.description: Top-ranked tennis player Alexander Zverev was officially notified of a lawsuit filed by his former partner during the middle of the season-ending ATP Finals.

item.title: ABC News: GWS Giants desperate to draft young star
item.description: Western Sydney product, Ethan Matthews is the ideal draftee for GWS — a local boy who's passionate about the Giants and wants to help grow the game of Australian Rules in rugby league heartland.

item.title: ABC News: Power surge leaves residents facing thousands in unexpected costs
item.description: Many Victorians are thousands of dollars out of pocket after a power surge in Mildura in September damaged household appliances, with some insurance claims rejected.

item.title: ABC News: Live: ASX to open lower as Wall Street braces for Anthropic IPO
item.description: The Aussie share market is set to open lower as Anthropic prepares to trade on the Nasdaq stock exchange. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

item.title: ABC News: Factory-built housing could lift construction productivity, report says
item.description: A new report from the Committee for Sydney think tank says housing construction productivity has gone backwards by 20 per cent since 2013.

item.title: ABC News: Bird backpacks and fresh poo used to track deadly H5 spread
item.description: A CSIRO program, which aims to better understand the H5 bird flu's impact, is using backpacks and bird poo to monitor the spread of the deadly virus in Australia's Murray Darling Basin.

item.title: ABC News: Opetaia's fight with former heavyweight champion called off
item.description: Jai Opetaia's eyebrow-raising move to heavyweight to fight Deontay Wilder is over after the Australian withdrew from their bout.

item.title: ABC News: Live: One in seven underpaid migrant workers took steps to recover wages, report finds
item.description: A report finds just one in seven underpaid migrant workers have taken steps to recover their wages. Follow live.

item.title: ABC News: Data centres could ignite a 'climate bomb' in Australia, report finds
item.description: The Climate Council has identified nine proposed data centres in Australia that could produce up to 40 million tonnes of pollution a year by 2035 if powered by fossil fuels.

item.title: ABC News: 'Exodus of talent': Video game developers leave NSW for better support
item.description: Screen NSW offers up to $30,000 per video game in state funding, but developers say it is not enough, and are leaving the state in search for better offers.

item.title: ABC News: CCTV stills show armed men in wild Melbourne brawl
item.description: Investigators say up to 20 people armed with baseball and cricket bats were involved in the early October brawl, which left one man with life-threatening injuries.

item.title: ABC News: Wet weather outbreak prompts paralysis tick warning
item.description: Predictive modelling shows about one in 20 visits to emergency vet clinics in Brisbane will be for paralysis ticks this summer.

item.title: ABC News: 'Own the crisis': Qld man's plea after near-death ambulance wait
item.description: A Queensland man who waited almost three hours for an ambulance while "bleeding out" is calling on the health minister to "own the crisis" in the wake of the deaths of three people.

item.title: ABC News: Whistleblower's 'disturbing' allegations probed by Canberra Health Services
item.description: Independent MLA Thomas Emerson told a Legislative Assembly hearing that Canberra Health Services surgery booking clerks were instructed to remove elective surgery patients from a waitlist if they had been waiting for more than 500 days.
